target: S2 increment 1 — typed contract at the brief seam for the flood service output (locks the #589 key contract)
findings_summary: Design: services return dicts (Trigger.dev consumers depend on that) so DON'T retype them; instead define a Pydantic contract for the EXPECTED flood output and parse the raw dict through it in _build_flood_detail. A renamed/missing key -> validation error (visible) not a silent null. flood_truth.run_flood emits epi_flood_class/epi_flood_label/jrc_water_occurrence_pct/dea_wofs_frequency_pct/bom_gauge_distance_km/flood_studies (+confidence/refused/reason). The brief's FloodDetail already reads the right keys post-#589; the contract makes a future drift fail loudly. Parse must be tolerant (model_validate, extra keys ignored) and must NOT crash the brief on a genuinely-absent field — only on a structural contract break. No service signature change; no DB.
model_design: FloodServiceOutput(BaseModel) with the documented emit keys as Optional; _build_flood_detail does FloodServiceOutput.model_validate(raw) then reads typed attributes; a validation error is caught and surfaced as NOT_AVAILABLE with the reason (fail-closed), AND logged loudly so contract drift is visible.
